row.question:
Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis for this 73-year-old woman with absence of breath sounds in the right hemithorax and mediastinal shift? Consider the presence of opacification, mediastinal shift, and absence of bronchial structures in your reasoning.
A) Total atelectasis of the right lung
B) Right-sided pneumonectomy
C) Unilateral pulmonary agenesis
D) Severe bronchiectasis with collapse
E) Right lung infection/pneumonia
F) Diaphragmatic hernia

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When a new unilateral hemithorax opacity appears after resolution of prior ipsilateral opacity, and mediastinal shift is toward the new opacity
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for loss of lung volume (flattened diaphragm, crowding of ribs, tracheal deviation) and absence of meniscus sign to favor atelectasis over effusion
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Fails if poor inspiration or overpenetration masks volume loss; does not differentiate mucus plugging from tumor/foreign body without clinical data

reflection_candidates.json.condition: When a homogeneous mediastinal opacity is seen lateral to the trachea on PA CXR and thyroid mass is considered
reflection_candidates.json.action: Inspect for continuity with cervical soft tissues and posterior spinal alignment on lateral view; absence of tracheal deviation and presence of cervicothoracic sign favor bronchogenic cyst
reflection_candidates.json.limitation: Requires lateral CXR; unreliable if opacity is small or obscured by overlying structures
